title: Mapped types
explain: A mapped type creates a new type by looping over the keys of another type. `[K in keyof T]` visits each key, and modifiers like `?`, `readonly` and `-readonly` add or remove flags. This is how `Partial`, `Readonly` and `Record` are built.
exercise: Write `Nullable<T>` that makes every property of `T` accept `null` as well.
tip: Mapped types are powerful but hard to read. Add a short comment with an example of the resulting type.
